resources.title: Gradient descent, how neural networks learn
resources.about: A video lesson with a text version: a network's cost function as a landscape, and learning as repeated steps down its negative gradient.
resources.use: When you want the picture of why training a model is walking downhill, before any algebra.

resources.title: Gradient descent
resources.about: A reference article: the update rule and its step size (learning rate), line searches, the linear least-squares case, and how the condition number slows it.
resources.use: For a quick reminder of the update rule, or the least-squares gradient, with links to the variants.

resources.title: Why Momentum Really Works
resources.about: An interactive article that splits gradient descent on a quadratic into eigen-directions, shows the step-size limit and the condition number at work, then adds momentum.
resources.use: When the eigenvalue view of step sizes and zig-zags needs to be seen moving, or for what momentum adds.

resources.title: Lecture 22: Gradient Descent: Downhill to a Minimum (18.065)
resources.about: Strang steps downhill on the bowl ½(x² + by²) and shows why a narrow bowl makes the path zig-zag slowly.
resources.use: For a lecture on gradient descent on a quadratic bowl from the linear-algebra side.

resources.title: Lecture 23: Accelerating Gradient Descent (Use Momentum) (18.065)
resources.about: The zig-zag example again, then momentum and Nesterov's method, which remember the previous step and converge faster on narrow bowls.
resources.use: When plain gradient descent is clear and the next question is how to beat the crawl on a narrow bowl.

resources.title: Lecture 25: Stochastic Gradient Descent (18.065)
resources.about: A guest lecture on stochastic gradient descent: a gradient from a random minibatch per step, fast early progress, and why it trains large models.
resources.use: For how gradient descent is actually run on big data sets in machine learning.

resources.title: Convex Optimization
resources.by: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe (Cambridge University Press, 2004)
resources.about: The standard textbook on convex optimization; the book's page links a free PDF of the whole text, with slides and exercises.
resources.use: For a careful treatment of descent methods and their convergence (chapter 9, unconstrained minimization), once the hand examples are solid.
